questions.q: A tablet batch has a test result in LIMS, a deviation in the eQMS and a hold status in SAP. Which system decides whether the stock can ship?
options: LIMS, because it holds the results
The eQMS, because it holds the deviation
SAP, through the batch status
Email, once QA sends approval
questions.why: Batch status in ERP usually controls whether stock can ship. It changes only after QA release.

questions.q: A sponsor outsources manufacturing to a CDMO. Who stays responsible for the product's quality?
options: The sponsor that owns the product
Only the CDMO, since it makes the product
The CRO running the trial
Whoever signed the purchase order
questions.why: The product owner keeps responsibility for quality. A quality agreement sets out who does which activity.

questions.q: Which ICH guideline is the GMP guide for active pharmaceutical ingredients?
options: ICH Q10
ICH E6
ICH Q9
ICH Q7
questions.why: ICH Q7 covers GMP for APIs. Q9 is quality risk management, Q10 is the pharmaceutical quality system and E6 is GCP.

questions.q: A lab analyst writes a result on a sticky note and types it into LIMS an hour later. Which ALCOA+ principles does this break?
options: Legible and enduring
Contemporaneous and original
Consistent and available
None, as long as the value is right
questions.why: The record was not made at the time of the activity, and the first record of the value was not kept.

questions.q: Batches with no deviation still wait eight days before release, mostly in QA review. The client asks for an AI report writer. What is the better first target?
options: A faster deviation report writer
More operators on the line
Batch record review by exception
A new LIMS with better reporting features
questions.why: The data shows the wait is in batch record review, so that is where the biggest saving is.

questions.q: Under 21 CFR 211.192, what must happen when a batch shows an unexplained discrepancy?
options: Investigate it and any other batches it may affect
Retest the samples until a passing result finally appears
Note it in the batch record and release as normal
Report it to FDA within one day and wait for advice
questions.why: The rule requires a thorough investigation that extends to other batches that may have been affected.

questions.q: A validation team tests every software function with full scripted tests, including report formatting. What would GAMP 5 and CSA suggest?
options: Test every function twice to be extra safe
Skip testing completely for vendor software
Only test after go-live using real batches
Focus effort on functions with higher risk
questions.why: Both push towards risk-based effort: deeper testing where failure could harm patients or product, lighter testing elsewhere.

questions.q: A QA manager says most deviation time is spent writing. Your date analysis shows long waits for lab data. What do you do?
options: Trust the manager and build a report writer
Show the data and discuss the lab hand-off
Ignore the lab since it is outside the project scope
Ask the lab manager to tell analysts to work faster
questions.why: Measure the waits before choosing a tool. The data points to an integration or hand-off problem, not writing.

questions.q: You are planning a gap assessment of the deviation process. What should you do first?
options: Set the scope and the requirements to assess against
Interview operators about their daily pain points
Draft the remediation plan and its budget for approval
Rank the gaps by effort so quick wins come first
questions.why: The scope and requirements define what 'gap' means. Everything else builds on them.

questions.q: Two root cause codes, 'Equipment' and 'Machine', mean the same thing. There is no direct GMP rule broken. Why rank it high for an AI project?
options: Inspectors always cite duplicate codes in every 483
It slows down the eQMS for every single user on site
It breaks trending and the data a model learns from
Duplicate codes are not allowed under the Part 11 rules
questions.why: Inconsistent categories block trending and give an AI tool confusing data, so they must be cleaned first.

questions.q: Which finding is a data integrity gap?
options: SOPs reviewed on a two-year cycle as the procedure says
Training records stored in a validated system
QA approval needed for CAPA closure
Two analysts share one login on an instrument
questions.why: Shared logins break 'attributable': you cannot tell who did what.

questions.q: How should you rank the gaps you found?
options: Patient and product risk first, then inspection risk
Easiest fixes first so the client sees progress quickly
In the order you found them during the site visits
By how many people mentioned each one in interviews
questions.why: Risk to patients and product comes first, even when the fix is hard.

questions.q: Your business case for a deviation assistant shows build and run cost only. What is missing?
options: The vendor's marketing and launch plan
Validation, SOPs, training and change control
The cost of the client's office space and power
Nothing, build and run are the full cost of the tool
questions.why: Regulated costs are real and QA and finance will look for them.

questions.q: Why does an AI assistant in GMP work usually save preparation time rather than review time?
options: Reviewers usually refuse to use AI drafts
Review is always quick, so there is little to save
AI cannot read GMP records stored in an eQMS
A qualified person must still review and sign
questions.why: The human approval step stays. The saving comes from searching, gathering and drafting.

questions.q: The CFO asks how much a lower chance of a warning letter is worth. What is the honest answer?
options: Quote a typical industry fine as the value
Multiply last year's revenue by a guessed risk factor
Describe the risk reduction, linked to specific gaps
Say it is worth nothing because it cannot be measured
questions.why: Do not invent a number. Describe the risk value plainly and link it to the gaps it closes.

questions.q: In the worked example, the low case is negative in year one. What does that mean?
options: The project should be cancelled before it starts
Validation and setup fall in year one; later years gain
The figures must be wrong and should be redone
The hourly cost should be raised until it turns positive
questions.why: One-time validation and setup costs land in year one. That is a normal, honest result.

questions.q: The client's eQMS vendor offers a licensed AI feature that covers most of the need. Which option should you look at first?
options: Configure the existing platform
Build a custom tool on a new cloud stack
Buy a second eQMS just for the AI part
Wait a year for a better model release
questions.why: Configuring an owned, validated platform can reuse its validation package and avoids duplicate tools.

questions.q: Under GAMP 5, which category usually needs the most validation effort?
options: Category 1, infrastructure
Category 3, standard software
Category 4, configured software
Category 5, custom software
questions.why: Custom software is not covered by a supplier's own testing, so more of the evidence must come from you.

questions.q: Who usually has the final say on whether a tool that touches GMP records is used?
options: The IT director
The procurement team
The head of quality
The AI vendor
questions.why: The quality unit is responsible for GMP records and can refuse any tool it cannot trust.

questions.q: A vendor's AI tool is impressive, but it cannot pin a version and updates itself monthly. Why is that a problem?
options: Monthly updates are too slow for a fast-moving site
Validated behaviour could change without control
The licence will cost more each month after updates
Users will dislike seeing new features every month
questions.why: If the tool changes without assessment and retesting, its validated state cannot be maintained.
